actions.detail: Safety-typed dispute with a chat message classified as a threat: rider asked to exit at 21:42 [F3]; driver replied at 21:43 "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4], flagged by the threat keyword filter [F5]; driver's statement alleges an uncorroborated door-opening on the expressway and admits he did not stop until Bedok Mall [F6]. claims.assertion: The driver's own in-app message at 21:43 reads "Sit down or I lock the doors", which the system tagged as a threat containing the keyword "lock the door" — i.e. intimidation directed at the passenger during the ride.

The rider asked to be let out of the car at 21:42 ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here") and the driver's threatening reply followed one minute later, so the intimidation was a response to the rider's request to exit, not to any aggression by her.

Because a threat/intimidation message appears in the chat record, this dispute must not be auto-adjudicated: the correct disposition is escalation to human review with a fact summary, not a fare ruling.
The driver's written statement admits he refused to stop and continued to the destination after the rider asked to get out, which corroborates that she remained in a vehicle she had asked to leave.

Both parties have clean 90-day dispute histories (rider 0 disputes / 0 upheld; driver 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days), so no account flag is requested against the rider and the escalation should be decided on the chat record itself.

weaknesses: The driver's statement (F6) asserts the rider was drunk and tried to open the door on the expressway, which, if credited, recasts "lock the doors" as a safety instruction rather than a threat — and chat/statements are the only evidence here, with no GPS or timeline record showing the door attempt or the rider's state.

There is no safety recording, no incident timeline and no medical or third-party evidence: F1 and F2 show only normal route and duration (15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal; 20.7 min vs 22 min estimated), so the GPS facts neither support nor contradict the threat claim.

The driver's profile is strong (F8: 5.8 years, 4.9 rating, 1204 trips, 0 disputes upheld), which the driver's side will use to argue the message was an isolated, justified instruction — though per the policy a profile fact can never decide the case alone.
No refund is legally computable here: the fare is a fixed RydeX quote with no fare facts in the file, so I cannot size any monetary remedy from a fare or GPS fact and seek escalation instead.

claims.assertion: The rider's chat message is an in-ride request to be let out mid-trip ('Please stop the car, I want to get out here.'), i.e. the dispute is about how the driver handled an in-motion request, not about any overcharge — the GPS record shows the trip was operated on the optimal route and slightly under it (15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal, -0%).

The driver's message was a safety instruction to remain seated with the doors secured, not an act of violence or a physical confinement: the rider was in a moving vehicle and the driver states she tried to open the door on the expressway, so telling her to sit down addresses an immediate risk in transit.

The trip was completed normally and safely: door-to-door duration was 20.7 min against a 22 min estimate (-1.1 min), and there is no traffic incident or route anomaly record — no erratic driving or delay evidence exists on the face of the system records.

The keyword flag at 21:43 is produced by automated keyword matching on a single message and cannot by itself establish a genuine threat; the policy's own definition covers 'Threats and Intimidation' as a conduct pattern, and a lone instruction to sit down falls short of that pattern.

The driver's account record is clean and long-standing — 5.8 years on platform, 4.9 rating, 1204 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld — which is inconsistent with a rider-safety hazard and supports that no safety measure against him is warranted.

The rider's own account shows no prior disputes (0 in 90 days, rating 4.8), so there is also no pattern of unfounded complaints on either side; the case turns on the single 21:42–21:43 exchange, which the driver's statement explains, and no refund of the fixed $32.86 fare is justified because the trip was performed as quoted on the optimal route.

weaknesses: F4 is verbatim a driver message containing a threat-classified phrase ('Sit down or I lock the doors.') and F5 confirms the threat keywords were detected, so the rider will argue this is a direct SAFE-1 trigger that must go to human escalation regardless of my safety rationale — I cannot make the flagged message disappear.

F6 is only the driver's own statement and is not corroborated by any GPS or timeline record of the rider attempting to open a door; under the system-records-win rule (F1, F2 alone show nothing unusual), the 'she tried to open the door on the expressway' account may be discounted, weakening D2.

The chat facts show the driver did not stop until Bedok Mall (F6 with F3), so on the face of the record he refused an explicit request to be let out mid-ride; policy RD-3(a) treats a passenger-named stop as a legitimate routing request, which the rider can invoke as evidence he did not comply.

I have no traffic/weather facts (tool returned none) and no fare facts to rebut the rider's account with objective corroboration, and I can only offer profile facts F7/F8 as background — the policy says profile facts cannot decide the case.

points.response: Conceded only as to the absence of any overcharge: the GPS record does show 15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal (F1), so I do not press RD-1 or any fare remedy — but that is irrelevant to a SAFE-1 safety dispute, and F3 still shows the rider asked to get out mid-ride at 21:42.

A normal distance and duration (F1, F2) says nothing about whether a threat was uttered; the rider's claim is about what was said and done to her inside the car, and F4/F5 record the flagged threat message, which SAFE-1 routes to escalation regardless of route or timing data.

The keyword hit (F5) is not asked to stand alone: the underlying verbatim driver message "Sit down or I lock the doors." (F4) is itself the conduct — a conditional threat of confinement, which the policy lists under Threats and Intimidation — and it was sent one minute after the rider asked to get out (F3), so it is a response to her request, not a neutral instruction.

The safety rationale rests entirely on the driver's own uncorroborated statement (F6); under the system-records-win rule there is no GPS, timeline or traffic fact in the file showing a door attempt or an expressway hazard to weigh against the verbatim message in F4, and the driver's own account admits he did not stop after the rider asked to get out (F3, F6).

The driver's clean record is background only (F8): the policy states profile facts can support a flag_account request but can never decide a case, so a 4.9 rating cannot neutralise a threat message that the system itself flagged (F5).

I accept that both sides have no prior disputes (F7, F8) and that no fare refund is at stake because the fixed RydeX quote was consistent with the route run (F1, F2); my ask is therefore not money but that the flagged threat (F4, F5) be escalated to human review rather than disposed of as no_action.

I do not dispute that F4 is verbatim and that F5 shows automated keyword matching; my point is that a keyword detection is not a finding of intimidation under SAFE-1, which speaks of 'Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind … Threats and Intimidation' as a conduct pattern, and the same tool that produced F5 also produced only one single message across the whole 21:34–21:55 trip.

C2 assumes the rider's request caused the message, but the chat shows only two messages one minute apart (F3, F4) and no context explaining why she asked to exit; the driver's statement (F6) supplies that reason — an attempted door opening on the expressway — so the causal story is contested, not established.

I concede that where a threat keyword appears in the chat record, SAFE-1 directs escalation rather than an automatic monetary ruling — I do not ask the judge to rule on the threat itself, only to record that the fare and route records show no overcharge or route violation supporting any refund.

F6 does record that the driver continued to the destination after F3, but the same statement explains he did so for her own safety after an attempt to open the door on an expressway; SAFE-2 escalation covers exactly this situation and no clause makes continuing to a destination, by itself, a basis for a refund.

I agree no flag is sought against the rider and that F7/F8 are background only; for symmetry the rider's clean record (F7) also means nothing is proved against the driver, whose record (F8: 5.8 years, 4.9, 1204 trips, 0 upheld) is inconsistent with the serious-safety-conduct finding C3 invites.

I withdraw the framing of D1 insofar as it suggests the rider's exit request has no policy weight: RD-3(a) does treat a passenger-named stop as a legitimate routing request, so I no longer rely on the request itself being irrelevant — the operational record (F1, F2) still shows no deviation or overcharge in the ride as performed.
